review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped for uses of the candidate lemmas in the repository. Two repeated-reasoning patterns hold up: the line-convexity lemma, which is proved twice, and the "rearranged vanishes outside the centered bound" argument, which is also proved twice. I rejected the other repeats as too short or routine under the rubric. Those were the `centered a = Ioo …` rewrite, the `le_total` case splits in `centered_inter` and `heightMeasure_centered_inter`, the symmetric hF'/hG' blocks in `fiberStar_difference`, and the indicator-lintegral computations. I could not run Lean, so the proposed rewrites are untested and I have only checked their types by reading. The second finding is weaker, because the shared lemma already exists and is unused.

findings.problem: `line_segment_mem` re-proves, by an explicit convex combination of the two endpoints, the fact that `{a | y + a • e ∈ K}` is convex along a line. It is exactly `line_interval_mem` (line 672) with r := c-1 and t := c+1. `line_interval_mem` proves the same fact more cleanly: it shows the preimage of K along the line is `Convex` and applies `OrdConnected`. The file therefore carries two independent proofs of one convexity-along-a-line statement. The weaker, special-case version sits about 600 lines earlier than the general one, and its `hz` is a conjunction rather than `Icc` membership.
findings.proposed_change: Move `line_interval_mem` (statement and proof, lines 672–681) up before `shifted_step`, inside the first `ShiftedSections` namespace section. It needs only `Convex ℝ K` and `Set.Icc`, and both `open Set` and the variable block `E` are already in scope there. Delete `line_segment_mem` (lines 61–67). In `shifted_step`, replace `line_segment_mem hK hcl hcr ?_` by `line_interval_mem hK hcl hcr (show q ∈ Icc (c-1) (c+1) from ⟨?_,?_⟩)`. The rewrite applies to both uses, at lines 85 and 87 (`z := q+1` and `z := q+(-1)`, with the bounds still discharged by `linarith [hcb.1,hcb.2,hqb.1,hqb.2]`). Alternatively, keep `line_segment_mem` as a one-line alias, `line_interval_mem hK hleft hright hz`, with `hz` unpacked as `⟨hz.1, hz.2⟩`, since `Icc` membership is definitionally the conjunction.
findings.benefit: The file would have one proof of convexity along a line, not two. The shared lemma would sit where it is first needed. A reader of `shifted_step` would see the general interval statement used by `section_mono`, `section_of_fiber_pair` and `shifted_step` alike. Maintenance would involve one proof, not two.

findings.problem: `rearranged_eq_zero_of_bound` (lines 339–346) proves that the rearrangement vanishes at s outside `centered L` when every `μ (S u) ≤ L`. It unfolds `rearranged layer`, shows each indicator is zero with `indicator_of_notMem`, and finishes with `simp only [he, lintegral_zero]`. `fiberStar_eq_zero_of_measure_le` repeats the same skeleton: unfold, a pointwise `indicator_of_notMem` fact `hz`, then `simp only [hz, lintegral_zero]`. It only adds a `toReal` computation to show `s ∉ centered (ofReal (2*|s|))`. The general lemma is never used (a grep finds no other reference), so the specialised copy has silently replaced it.
findings.proposed_change: Prove `fiberStar_eq_zero_of_measure_le` from `rearranged_eq_zero_of_bound`. Use `S := superlevel (fun r => F (x,r))`, `L := ENNReal.ofReal (2*|s|)`, `hL := ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top`, and `hbound := h`. For `hs : s ∉ centered L`, `change` to `¬ |s| < (ENNReal.ofReal (2*|s|)).toReal/2`, rewrite with `ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (by positivity)`, and close with `linarith`/`lt_irrefl`. The unfold-and-indicator-vanishing argument then appears once. Since `fiberStar F (x,s)` is definitionally `rearranged (superlevel …) volume volume s`, a `show`/`exact` suffices. The `omit [MeasurableSpace X]` can stay. The general lemma is already stated without the `SFinite` hypotheses, so it applies to `volume` on ℝ.
findings.benefit: The file would have one proof that `rearranged` is zero outside a bound. The currently dead lemma would become the single place that handles the indicator and lintegral reasoning. `fiberStar_eq_zero_of_measure_le` would then reduce to the real-number step `|s| < ofReal(2|s|).toReal/2` being false.
